tour.subtitle: A private day on the island of the Colossus with a licensed guide and car: the walled Old Town of the Knights of St John, the Street of the Knights and the Palace of the Grand Master, the coast road south, the white village of Lindos and its acropolis high above the sea, and a swim in St Paul's Bay.

tour.overview:
Rhodes has been a crossroads of the Mediterranean for three thousand years. In antiquity, its harbour was guarded by the Colossus, a bronze statue of the sun god Helios more than 30 metres tall, one of the Seven Wonders of the World. In 1309 the island was taken by the Knights of St John, who turned the town into a fortress against the Ottoman Empire and held it until 1522. Their walled city, with its palace, inns and gates, is the best-preserved medieval town in Europe and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988.

This private day combines the Old Town with the island's most beautiful village, with a licensed guide and a car. In the morning you walk through the Old Town and the Palace of the Grand Master. After a drive down the east coast, you climb to the acropolis of Lindos, where a temple of Athena overlooks two bays, have lunch and swim at St Paul's Bay, and wander the lanes of the village.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel on Rhodes or the cruise port
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; about 5 km, with a steep climb of about 15 minutes to the acropolis of Lindos

WHAT YOU SEE
• Rhodes Old Town: the Street of the Knights, the Palace of the Grand Master, Hippocrates Square and the walls.
• Mandraki harbour.
• The village of Lindos.
• The acropolis of Lindos and the Temple of Athena Lindia.
• St Paul's Bay.

WHY THIS WORKS
We see the Old Town early, before the cruise crowds, and reach Lindos after the morning coaches have left, with a car waiting at the bottom of the hill.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, couples, history lovers and cruise passengers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer nature, ask us for a day to the Valley of the Butterflies and the mountain villages of the interior.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The acropolis of Lindos is hot and shadeless in summer; we can visit it first or last to avoid the midday sun. Donkeys carry visitors up the hill; we recommend walking instead, for the animals' welfare.

days.name: Rhodes Old Town, the Palace of the Grand Master, Mandraki, Lindos and its acropolis, and St Paul's Bay
days.description:
What to expect: the city of the Knights and the most beautiful village of Rhodes, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets, lunch and a swim.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel or at the cruise port at about 8:30. You enter the Old Town through the walls, four kilometres long and up to 12 metres thick, with moats and gates built by the Knights. You walk up the Street of the Knights, the best-preserved medieval street in Europe, lined with the inns where the knights of each 'Tongue' – France, Italy, Spain, England and others – lodged and dined. At the top stands the Palace of the Grand Master, destroyed by an explosion in 1856 and rebuilt by the Italians in the 1930s as a residence for Mussolini; inside, the halls are paved with Roman and early Christian mosaics brought from the island of Kos. You continue through the lanes of the lower town, past the Suleiman Mosque, to Hippocrates Square, and look out over Mandraki harbour, where bronze deer stand on columns at the entrance, the spot where tradition places the Colossus.

You drive about an hour down the east coast to Lindos, a village of whitewashed houses and pebble-mosaic courtyards below a rock 116 metres high. You climb the path to the acropolis, entering through the castle of the Knights, past a relief of a Greek warship carved into the rock around 180 BC, to the Doric Temple of Athena Lindia and its stoa, with dizzying views over the turquoise bays on both sides.

Lunch is at St Paul's Bay, an almost enclosed lagoon where the apostle Paul is said to have landed in 51 AD, with time to swim in the clear water. You then wander through the lanes of Lindos, visit the Church of the Panagia with its frescoes, and see the 17th-century captains' houses with their carved doorways. Your driver takes you back to your hotel or ship at about 16:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up at your hotel or the port.
08:45 – Rhodes Old Town and the Street of the Knights.
09:45 – Palace of the Grand Master.
11:00 – Mandraki harbour.
11:15 – Drive to Lindos.
12:15 – Acropolis of Lindos.
13:30 – Lunch and swim at St Paul's Bay.
15:15 – Village of Lindos.
16:30 – Back at your hotel or ship.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Palace of the Grand Master is closed on some holidays; we then visit the Archaeological Museum in the Hospital of the Knights.
• Cruise passengers: we plan to have you back at least one hour before all-aboard time.
• The order of the day can be reversed to see Lindos at its coolest.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Palace of the Grand Master and acropolis of Lindos tickets, lunch, bottled water, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: sunbeds, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can you pick us up from the cruise ship?
faq.answer: Yes. The cruise port is right next to the Old Town. We plan the day so you are back at least one hour before all-aboard time.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the Palace of the Grand Master and the acropolis of Lindos.

faq.question: How hard is the climb in Lindos?
faq.answer: About 15 minutes up a steep stepped path from the village. Take your time; there are places to rest and shade on the way.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch at St Paul's Bay or in Lindos. Vegetarian and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Can we swim?
faq.answer: Yes, at St Paul's Bay. Bring a swimsuit and towel.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the castle walls, the knights' stories and the swim. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The Old Town has cobbles and the palace has stairs; the acropolis of Lindos is reached only on foot. The coastal scenery and St Paul's Bay are easy.

faq.question: Do you use the donkeys in Lindos?
faq.answer: No. We recommend walking, for the animals' welfare. If you cannot climb, we enjoy Lindos from below and add another stop.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes with grip, a hat, sun cream and a swimsuit.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to June and September to October. Rhodes has warm seas into November; July and August are hot and busy.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
